tomato_early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
tomato_early_blight.description: Early blight is a major fungal disease affecting tomato plants worldwide, causing foliage loss and significant crop damage if left untreated.
symptoms: Concentric dark brown target-spot rings on older lower leaves.
Yellow chlorotic halo around leaf lesions.
Lower foliage wilting and premature leaf drop.
causes: Fungal spores (Alternaria solani) surviving in plant debris or soil.
High humidity combined with warm temperatures (24°C - 29°C).
organicTreatment: Spray Neem oil solution (5ml/L water) or copper soap biopesticide every 7-10 days.
Prune affected lower leaves and dispose of them outside the farm.
Mulch soil around base with straw to stop fungal spore splash.
chemicalTreatment: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP or Chlorothalonil fungicide spray.
Alternate active ingredients to prevent fungal resistance.
preventionTips: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Use drip irrigation instead of sprinkler systems.
Maintain adequate spacing between plants for ventilation.
tomato_early_blight.recommendedFertilizer: Potassium-rich organic compost and balanced N-P-K (10-10-10) with micronutrients.
tomato_early_blight.waterRequirement: Moderate drip irrigation twice a week (avoid wetting foliage).
tomato_early_blight.precautions: Avoid handling plants when leaves are wet to prevent spreading spores.
tomato_early_blight.immediateAction: Isolate the plant, cut off heavily infected bottom foliage immediately, and apply organic neem oil.
tomato_early_blight.speechText: Diagnosis: Tomato Early Blight. Scientific name: Alternaria solani. Symptoms include dark brown concentric spots and yellowing leaves. Organic treatment: Prune lower leaves and apply neem oil. Chemical treatment: Apply Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil.

corn_common_rust.name: Corn Common Rust
corn_common_rust.description: Common rust is a airborne fungal disease in maize characterized by reddish-brown pustules on leaves.
symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Powdery rust spores rubbing off easily on touch.
Premature leaf yellowing and reduced photosynthetic yield.
causes: Wind-blown urediniospores from infected host crops.
Cool temperatures (16°C - 23°C) and heavy dew exposure.
organicTreatment: Dust sulfur powder or spray bio-fungicide containing Bacillus subtilis.
Ensure proper crop spacing and weed management.
chemicalTreatment: Apply Azoxystrobin or Propiconazole foliar sprays if canopy coverage exceeds 10%.
preventionTips: Destroy leftover crop residue promptly after harvest.
corn_common_rust.recommendedFertilizer: Balanced Nitrogen and Potash soil application.
corn_common_rust.waterRequirement: Regular furrow irrigation with good field drainage.
corn_common_rust.precautions: Do not over-fertilize with excessive nitrogen.
corn_common_rust.immediateAction: Monitor canopy rust density. If pustules spread rapidly, apply sulfur or recommended foliar fungicide.
corn_common_rust.speechText: Diagnosis: Corn Common Rust. Scientific name: Puccinia sorghi. Symptoms include cinnamon brown pustules. Organic treatment: Dust sulfur or Bacillus subtilis. Chemical treatment: Apply Azoxystrobin spray.

potato_late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
potato_late_blight.description: Late blight is an aggressive oomycete pathogen capable of destroying entire potato crops rapidly in damp weather.
symptoms: Water-soaked dark green to black leaf spots starting at leaf tips.
White cottony downy fungal growth on lower leaf surface under moisture.
Foul odor and rapid foliage breakdown.
causes: High relative humidity (>90%) and cool ambient temperatures (12°C - 20°C).
Infected seed tubers carrying dormant sporangia.
organicTreatment: Apply Copper hydroxide or Bordeaux mixture thoroughly.
Uproot and destroy severely infected potato vines immediately.
chemicalTreatment: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb or Dimethomorph systemic fungicide.
preventionTips: Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers.
Hill up soil high around plant bases to shield developing tubers from spores.
potato_late_blight.waterRequirement: Soil moist but well-drained. Avoid waterlogging.
potato_late_blight.precautions: Destroy infected haulms before harvesting tubers.
potato_late_blight.immediateAction: Immediately remove infected plants and spray copper or systemic fungicides across the plot.
potato_late_blight.speechText: Diagnosis: Potato Late Blight. Scientific name: Phytophthora infestans. Symptoms: Water soaked dark leaf spots with white underside mold. Organic treatment: Apply copper hydroxide. Chemical treatment: Spray Metalaxyl with Mancozeb.

healthy_crop.name: Healthy Crop Leaf
healthy_crop.description: The leaf shows vibrant pigmentation, healthy cellular structure, and zero signs of fungal, bacterial, or pest infection.
symptoms: No spots, necrotic spots, or fungal lesions.
causes: Good agricultural practices, balanced nutrition, and optimal moisture.
organicTreatment: No chemical or organic disease treatment required.
Maintain organic soil compost and vermicompost application.
chemicalTreatment: None needed. Protect beneficial soil organisms.
preventionTips: Continue regular crop field monitoring every 3-5 days.
Ensure proper weed control and crop sanitation.
healthy_crop.recommendedFertilizer: Organic vermicompost or liquid bio-fertilizer every 3 weeks.
healthy_crop.precautions: Avoid over-watering and maintain proper soil aeration.
healthy_crop.immediateAction: No treatment required! Continue routine healthy crop care.
healthy_crop.speechText: Great news! Your crop leaf is completely healthy with no disease detected. Continue regular watering and compost care.
